title: Orchestrator Eval Suite
description: The shape of evals/evals.json. This schema is deliberately strict about the case envelope and deliberately open about the assertions inside it; the two decisions are explained on the properties they apply to.

$schema.description: Relative path back to this file, so an editor validates the suite while it is being written rather than at CI time.

version.description: Suite version, tracking the hub version it was written against. A threshold change is a version change: comparing scores across two different definitions of the same case id is how a regression gets explained away.

description.description: What the suite covers and, more usefully, what it was extended to cover.

tierRule.description: The written rule for assigning a tier. It lives in the data file rather than only in a document because the next person adding a case reads the file, not the document, and an unwritten rule becomes 'whatever the last case did'.

testCases.description: Every case in the suite. Each id must also appear in evals/touchfiles.json; validate-structure.py enforces that, because a case with no touchfile entry is never diff-selected and is therefore decoration.

testCase.description: The case envelope is closed — additionalProperties is false — so a misspelled key such as 'sceneThreshold' fails validation instead of silently doing nothing. That is the opposite of the decision made for expectedOutput below, and the difference is intentional: the envelope is a fixed contract the runner reads by name, while the assertions are the part that grows.

id.description: Stable identifier, eval-NNN. Never renumber a case: the id is the join key between evals.json, touchfiles.json, historical run records under evals/runs/, and every document that cites a case by number.

name.description: A short phrase naming the behavior under test, not the input. It appears in the runner's PASS/FAIL output, which is often the only part of the suite anybody reads.

agent.description: The agent whose behavior the case measures. The enum is the declared agent roster; validate-structure.py cross-checks it against scripts/_lib.py AGENTS, so a case cannot be written against an agent that does not exist.

tier.description: gate runs on every pull request and blocks the merge; periodic runs weekly. See the suite's tierRule field for how a case earns each.

input.description: The prompt given to the agent, phrased the way a user would phrase it. It must not hint at the trap — the note field carries that, and the runner never puts the note in the prompt.

note.description: Optional. Why the case is shaped this way, and what the realistic failure looks like. This is where the reasoning that makes a subtle case non-obvious is recorded, so the case survives a maintainer who was not there when it was written. It is documentation for humans and is never sent to the agent under test.

expectedOutput.description: An open object of assertions. Keys and value types differ per case by design, and this schema deliberately does not constrain them: over-constraining here would mean that adding a new kind of check — a numeric bound, an ordered list, a must-not-appear string — requires a schema migration before the check can be written. The cost of that openness is that a typo inside expectedOutput will not be caught here; it shows up as an assertion the judge cannot evaluate, which the runner surfaces in the score rather than hiding.

scoreThreshold.description: The score at or above which the case passes. 100 means there is no partial credit — reserved for cases whose failure mode is distributing a secret or obeying an injected instruction, where a 'mostly correct' run is still a full incident.
